citations.claim: body1 at waypoint before failure, x finite
body1 at waypoint before failure, y finite
body1 position becomes non-finite (null) at violating step
total energy becomes non-finite at same step

counterfactual.change: Set controller.enabled from true to false. This removes waypoint-direction division by zero; scenario then runs 1228 steps with no violation.

explanation: Controller body 1 sits exactly on its waypoint by step 1227 with near-zero velocity. At step 1228 position/velocity become null. With controller disabled the same scenario runs fine, indicating controller force calculation divides by distance-to-waypoint (zero) when waypoint is reached, producing NaN that propagates to state and energy.
vision_note: Steps 1225 to 1227 show a red violating body stationary near the top with blue bodies near the floor and a single waypoint at top-right. At step 1228 the red body vanishes entirely and a second waypoint appears near its former position while blue bodies remain. [disagreement: Legend says orange=controller body, red=violator, but no orange body is visible and no body is on the top-right waypoint at 1227. The explanation claims the controller body itself is on the waypoint at 1227 and then becomes null, but the image shows the controller is not at the waypoint and the body that disappears is the separate red violator, suggesting NaN propagation rather than direct controller-on-waypoint visualization.]
